sections.html:
Lehi is a city in Utah County at the northern end of Utah Valley, and it is part of the Provo and Orem metropolitan area. The city covers about 28 square miles at an elevation of roughly 4,561 feet.

The Corporate Center on Traverse Mountain, the historic Main Street downtown and the Thanksgiving Point complex are the three areas most often named in reference sources.

Climate matters for a house here. The mean daily high in July is about 90 degrees and the mean low in January is about 16 degrees. Annual precipitation averages around 12 inches, which is dry, but winter cold stresses water lines and older furnaces.

sections.h2: How did Lehi go from a pioneer settlement to a fast-growing city?
sections.html:
Pioneers settled the Lehi area in fall 1850 at a place called Dry Creek, and the Utah Territorial Legislature incorporated Lehi City on February 5, 1852, making it the sixth city incorporated in Utah. Before that the settlement carried other names, including Sulphur Springs, Snow's Springs and Evansville.

Lehi stayed small for a century. The census low was 2,733 in 1940, and the count was still only 8,475 in 1990. Then growth picked up fast.

  • 2000: 19,028 residents
  • 2010: 47,407 residents
  • 2020: 75,907 residents
  • July 2025 estimate: 95,313 (Census Bureau)

The 2020 median age was 26.2, and about 39.5 percent of residents were under 18. A younger, larger household profile means family-sized homes are the norm in much of the city, and an older house in the original grid can look very different from a subdivision built a few years ago.

Lehi's historic core is the Lehi Main Street Historic District, which is on the National Register of Historic Places. The Lehi Roller Mills, built by a farmers' cooperative in 1906, were listed in 1994 and appeared in the 1984 film Footloose.

sections.h2: What jobs shape the Lehi housing market?
sections.html:
Lehi moved from farming to a technology economy that is part of the area called Silicon Slopes. Reference sources name Micron, which began a chip plant that became IM Flash Technologies, and Texas Instruments announced its purchase of the facility in June 2021.

Other employers on the list include Adobe, Ancestry.com, which has been headquartered in Lehi since 2016, Vivint, Microsoft and Oracle. Lehi's first hospital opened in June 2015, and Thanksgiving Point, a museum and garden complex founded in 1995, draws about 1.45 million visitors a year.

Owners who bought during a hiring wave can run into a layoff, a remote work shift or a job offer elsewhere. In those cases the main challenge is timing, since a mortgage payment continues while the house waits for a buyer.

sections.h2: How do roads and rail connect Lehi to Salt Lake City and Provo?
sections.html:
Interstate 15 runs through Lehi with five exits, and that is the main reason many households choose the city. FrontRunner South commuter rail opened its Lehi station on December 12, 2012, near Thanksgiving Point, and Utah Transit Authority operates local buses.

Distance to an I-15 ramp or the rail station is something a buyer's agent will price in. A house on the far side of the city from the interstate may attract a different buyer than one near the Corporate Center.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Lehi homes?
sections.html:
Lehi public schools have been run by Alpine School District, which includes Lehi High and Skyridge High. That is changing. Alpine School District will cease to exist in July 2027 and be replaced by three new districts, one of which is named Aspen Peaks.

The articles reviewed did not say which new district will serve each Lehi address, so a seller with a buyer asking about schools should confirm the boundary for the exact property with the district or the city. Mountainland Technical College has a Lehi campus offering automotive, culinary, healthcare and IT training.

sections.h2: What city rules should a Lehi seller know about?
sections.html:
Lehi's Building and Inspections Department issues all building permits, and any open permit or unfinished work can delay a closing. Applications go through an online submittal portal, and the city says current codes include the 2021 I-Codes and the 2020 National Electrical Code with Utah amendments.

  • Call 385-201-1035 to schedule an inspection, and give at least 24 hours notice. Inspections are not scheduled by voicemail, email or online.
  • Have the work ready first. Re-inspection fees apply if a project clearly is not.
  • Look up status by permit number, site address or subdivision and lot.

Lehi also runs a pressurized irrigation system that supplies untreated water for yards and city fire hydrants. A city ordinance prohibits irrigation water use after October 15, owners turn the connection on and off each year, and the city says it is currently in Phase 2 of its Water Shortage Management Plan. Buyers moving in from elsewhere often ask how the yard is watered, so a seller can explain the connection and watering schedule up front. Lehi City is at 131 N 100 E, phone (385) 201-1000.

sections.h2: How do Utah County valuation notices, tax bills and recording work for a Lehi sale?
sections.html:
Utah County mails valuation notices in the summer, sends tax notices in October and collects taxes by 5:00 pm on November 30. The county's sample notice from 2022 shows an appeal deadline of September 15 for that year, and appeals go to the Utah County Board of Equalization through the Auditor at 111 S. University Ave, Provo, or by phone at (801) 851-8109, option 3.

The valuation notice is not a tax bill. Actual amounts due appear in the October tax notice, so a seller closing in the fall should ask the title company how that year's taxes are being prorated.

Deeds are recorded with the Utah County Recorder at 100 East Center St, Suite 1300, Provo. The recorder's fee page lists $40 per document, but the Cache County site reports that state law raised county recording fees by $5 starting May 6, 2026, so ask for the current figure before closing.

sections.h2: Does the Utah primary residence exemption follow a Lehi house to the next owner?
sections.html:
No, the exemption does not transfer automatically. Utah gives a 45 percent exemption on the market value of a primary home, so taxable value is 55 percent, and the Utah State Tax Commission says the owner must live in the home at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year.

After a sale or deed transfer, the new owner files Form TC-473A with the county Board of Equalization by September 15, and counties cannot take late filings. A buyer who misses the date can be taxed on the full market value for that year. Owners of rentals file a residential declaration signed by all owners instead, and second or vacation homes do not qualify.

Telling a buyer about that deadline in advance is a courtesy that avoids a surprise tax bill after a fall closing.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Lehi house?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Lehi uses the same title and recording steps, and the buyer does not need lender approval. A title company searches for liens, the parties sign, and the deed is recorded in Provo.

  • Tell the buyer about the house, its condition and your timeline.
  • Compare the offer and closing date with a listing plan.
  • Clear any open permits or liens before the closing date.
  • Sign and receive the proceeds after payoffs and prorated taxes.

That path suits owners who inherited a Lehi house, who are behind on payments, or whose house needs work they do not want to finance.

faqs.q: How many people live in Lehi, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 95,313 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 75,907, up from 47,407 in 2010.

faqs.q: When are Utah County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by 5:00 pm on November 30. Utah County mails tax notices in October, and a valuation notice is not a bill.

faqs.q: What is the Utah County appeal deadline for a Lehi property valuation?
faqs.a: The county's sample valuation notice listed September 15 as the deadline. Check the current notice for the year, since the date printed on it governs.

faqs.q: Will Alpine School District still serve Lehi?
faqs.a: Not after July 2027. Alpine School District will be replaced by three new districts, and Lehi sellers should confirm the district for a specific address before telling buyers.

faqs.q: Who inspects building work in Lehi?
faqs.a: The city's Building and Inspections Department does. Call 385-201-1035 at least 24 hours ahead to schedule an inspection.
